A Creo Mentem spell that sparks conscience to remove the Obsession Personality Trait imposed by a demon's obsession power.

A Summer covenant of medium power occupying a large castle and serving as Mundane Lord of the local village, keeping a low profile in Hermetic politics and offering generous hospitality to visiting magi and Redcaps.
A Tytalus magus of peasant stock at Castrum Antiquum who used Herbam, Auram and Animál magic to wring great harvests from poor northern land.
Son of the seer Emrys, adopted as Quendalon's apprentice; of strong faerie heritage, he became a master of symbolic prediction and founder of the Heirs to Merlin lineage.
A Rhine political gild founded by western covenants seeking to push the limits of the Code through mundane dealings; described disparagingly as a front for mundane meddling.

A General, Minor Virtue: the character was trained in the New Aristotle, gaining +1 to Artes Liberales rolls for grammar, logic, rhetoric, +1 to Disputatio Totals, and (for magi) +1 to relevant Lab Totals.
Possibly the most brilliant magus in the tribunal, a Jerbiton at Schola Pythagoranis devoted to natural philosophy who critiques magic theory's physics.
Author of The Canon of Medicine, quoted as the defining text on medicine as a science of the human body's dispositions.
A laboratory Flaw present after only the first season of a standard lab's setup, giving a –3 penalty to all Lab Totals until the second setup season removes it.
The maga who was Flavius of Jerbiton's teacher, collected him from the Alps, and negotiated with Trianoma to bring Eastern Empire magi into the Order; she died in 763 before the First Tribunal.
A Creo Ignem spell (Level 15) that forms fire along a metal blade, doubling the weapon's damage (or adding +5) and starting fires; repeated castings can melt the blade.
An Intellego Mentem spell letting the caster see through the eyes of a person to whom he has an Arcane Connection.
A Minor Social Status Virtue for a priest of a crusading order, answerable only to the pope outside the order.
A Virtue suggested for Mithraic characters of House Flambeau.
A strictly cloistered monastic order, the extreme example of monastic insularity.
A branch of the royal court headed by the chancellor Richard de Marsh, responsible for issuing documents under the Great Seal and keeping government records such as the Pipe Rolls.
A Major Sanguine Disease afflicting women who have just given birth, caused by the it demon.
The 'Protect' clan of House Bjornaer, the most active Harmonist clan and protectors of all Bjornaer magi, which absorbed most ninth-century Merinita defectors.
A spell that makes a ghost obey the caster as long as it can be coerced with threats such as defiling its grave or banishing it to Hell.
entity: Coerce the Spirits of the Night

text: A Rego Imaginem spell (Level 30) that makes the target see everything vibrate and hear displaced sounds, imposing -3 on Attack and Defense and extra botch dice.
An Unseelie faerie court associated with dark, fire, warmth, and agriculture, found in midsummer in the swampy Hunsruck forest west of the Rhine Gorge; rival to Bright Winter.
A Minor Hermetic Flaw: the magus has problems creating new things in the lab, taking -3 to Lab Totals unless using a Laboratory Text or being taught.
A Perdo Corpus spell (Level 25) that inflicts leprosy on the target, causing an Incapacitating Wound and loss of Stamina as the flesh rots.
Non-Hermetic Thessalian wizards who did not join the Order, dwelling in the Cambunian Mountains; suspected of diabolism and demon worship.
An alchemist Criamon magus, teacher of the current Prima Muscaria, whose carnal urges are embodied in the captured adulteration called the Carnal Wolf.
A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab is configured for an especially small magus, causing difficulty for normal-sized users.
One of the two major new mendicant friar orders of the early thirteenth century, growing rapidly in popularity.
A Major General Flaw making the character the size of a child, with Size -2 and penalties to Strength and Stamina.
A Major, Hermetic Virtue letting a magus manipulate the elemental Forms (Aquam, Auram, Ignem, Terram) as a connected whole, sharing experience among them.
A Minor, General Virtue allowing a character to withstand pain and fatigue, reducing Fatigue and wound penalties and granting +3 to resist pain.
The Ability central to Jerbiton 'tasteful living,' used to convey symbolic messages, make individual impressions at events, and force rivals into faux pas.
A Free laboratory Structure Flaw: the building is partially it to the elements, e.g. unroofed or wind-cracked (-1 Safety, +1 Upkeep, -2 Health, -1 Aesthetics, +1 Auram).
A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character was raised by faeries, gaining enhanced understanding of magic and faeries but finding human society bizarre.
A Minor, Supernatural Virtue for a bird-shifter who can separate a feather and telepathically control it as a self-inking quill, associated with the Daughters of Four Fathers.
A leadership title of the Seirenes won at a grand competition every 12 years, treated equally to the other Firsts.
A House Merinita lineage and Mystery Cult descended from it who Initiate the illusion Mysteries of Spell Timing, Glamour, and Perpetuity.
A trading city founded by Charlemagne at the 'Ford of the Franks' on the River Main, home to about 10,000 citizens and host of imperial elections.
A region of southwestern France, the probable birthplace of Flambeau the Founder around 715 AD.
A bound ghost covenfolk template with Magic Might 10 (Mentem), insubstantial and invisible, that stands watch over a covenant; bound magically rather than haunting.
The treasure the Argonauts voyaged to retrieve, during which Orpheus saved them from the sirens.
A Virtue providing an exceptionally high Dexterity Characteristic, taken by the glass-blower and burglar templates.
An example famous maestro affiliated with the Divine realm, commissioned to paint a wall mural for the bishop of Milan.
The Burgundian king of Worms in the Nibelungenlied, who marries Brünhild with Siegfried's help and is later beheaded by Kriemhild in Hungary.
A Minor, Hermetic Virtue giving great control over one's spells, allowing the magus to cancel his own spells and magic items by concentrating.
A former king of England whose reign featured William Marshal's early career, the Henry of Essex duel, and afforestations later restricted by the Charter of the Forest.
A gathering of the Order held in a vast twelve-sided quartz-walled hall in the Alps, supported by impossible ivory trees.

A famous Benedictine abbess and polymath (theology, medicine, music) of the 12th century, founder of Rupertsberg monastery; said to have been admitted to House Jerbiton as a pious unGifted Larta maga.
A Major Supernatural Flaw in which the character has snake-like tails instead of legs, a deformity that can be hidden under clothing but not while moving.
A Mystery House of magical craftsmen who enchant items through it magic, bound by oaths of secrecy and rivalry in their contests of craft.
A Rego Aquam spell (Level 35) that turns part of a body of water into jagged ice chunks that pound against anything on the surface, damaging swimmers and small boats.
A Minor Story Tainted Flaw in which a minor demon poses as a friend of the character to guide him toward a tragic destiny.
A Minor, Supernatural, Tainted Virtue giving the character a magical item inherited from a diabolist, useful but drawing its owner toward a demon.
An enchanted item prepared with Vim vis and then instilled with magical effects in the laboratory; variants include lesser enchanted devices and it, and an it lasts years as an Arcane Connection.
The master of Tabanus and the leading Traditionalist within House Guernicus, favoring a strict interpretation of the Code.
A Minor, General Virtue letting a character who briefly looks about a room detect and remember anything of interest without Awareness checks.
A king of England who summoned Eadric Wilde and his faerie wife to London out of a wish to look upon them.
A double line of hills on the Saxony-Thuringia border, legendary resting place of famous kings (notably Frederick Barbarossa) and site of Fengheld's Turris Acontiarum chapter.
The crusader-created state ruling Constantinople after the 1204 sack, the weakest of four powers feuding over the Balkans, whose Latin Emperor cares more for his home Flanders than the City.
A Major General Flaw representing the divine disease; it gives a permanent -2 Living Condition modifier and an extra Heavy Wound during Aging Crises, and prevents gaining a positive reputation.
A Virtue improving fine manual work; held by the Craftsman template and offered as an alternative for the Spying Maid.
A river near whose mouth an island was a college for Druidic priestesses in the years before the formation of the Order.
A city in northern Italy granted a charter by Henry IV in 1081, overthrown in a commune revolt in 1115, which has since conquered neighboring lands and rivals Pisa.
A Major Hermetic Flaw in which the magus craves casting magic and struggles to stop casting spells until he drops from exhaustion.
The domus magna of House Guernicus, in the Roman Tribunal, where Prima Bilera resides.
A magus of House Tytalus who collects turtle shells inscribed with bellicose Latin quotations.
A Creo Mentem spell (Level 20) that inserts a full false memory into a person's mind, revealed as false on a successful Intelligence roll; the memory vanishes when the duration expires.
One of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Lead,' founder of Clan it, whose name means 'mead-wolf' (bear) in Old Gothic.
A creature serving as a Local Ally for the Military Camp covenant situation, also referenced as a covenant Boon.
A Major General Flaw in which the character cannot speak; magi with this Flaw take a -10 penalty to all spellcasting unless offset by the Quiet Magic Virtue.
A covenant of nature magi founded in the East Anglian fens in 1133, destroyed by Geoffrey de Mandeville during the Civil War in 1143.
A Major General Flaw in which the character has it; magi take a -5 penalty to all Casting Scores, offset by the Subtle Magic Virtue or Still Casting.
A Rhine Tribunal covenant based in Lubeck, dominated by Jerbiton magi and merchants and lacking a Magic aura at its city site; deeply involved in commerce and the genesis of the Hanseatic League.
A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character has unshakable faith in his own abilities and cannot imagine failure.
A major Social Status Virtue for a character with a large financial stake in a wealthy company, providing minor-noble-level income and the ability to act in any company role except capo.
A Minor General Virtue granting +6 to rolls to avoid falling or tripping, especially on narrow ledges or tightropes.
A Creo Imaginem spell (Level 25) that makes an image of a clothed, equipped person that can move, speak, and behave as a human under the caster's unspoken command.
A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character is a fervent follower of his religion, avoiding what it prohibits and doing what it commands.
A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character has a very hard time recalling one type of thing such as names, faces, or places.
A supernatural Virtue granting forewarning of danger; Lord Robert Schonburg uses it to know when he is in trouble or about to be exposed.
A Profession Ability used (with Presence) to compute the loyalty bonus contributed by a Chamberlain specialist.
A Virtue granting a bonus to the Intrigue Ability, taken by the Political Agent template.
A Muto Auram spell (Level 20) that turns falling rain into small stones causing minor damage; the stones revert to water when the spell expires.
A faerie wolf with Faerie Might 12 and a ruddy neck and back; the messenger of the Winter Court who accompanies Torven and conveys the court's wishes to Waldheim.
A Creo Vim spell that temporarily restores faded spell traces to a fresh state so they can be examined.
A Creo Mentem spell (Level 15) that makes the target furious at someone or something of the caster's choice; an appropriate Personality Trait roll can hold the anger in check.
A special low price that royalty expects when buying at fairs, effectively a tax on the seller; King Henry III's Westminster fair promised to drop these prises.
One of the patron saints of glassmakers, whose feast day is April 25.

A covenant in the Transylvanian Tribunal that is a school for future apprentices, agents, and companions, set in an intermittently accessible regio and reputed to be a school for sorcerers run by the devil.

An angel of the Divine realm (Divine Might 50, Corpus) with special responsibility for Hermetic magi, sometimes drawing them closer to God and sometimes acting as the instrument of God's vengeance. He can duplicate any Hermetic effect and is the suggested antagonist for the Plagued by Angel Story Flaw.
A distant eastern land the Romans called the source of the finest silks and spices, from which Europe imports luxuries by paying tons of silver through Arabic intermediaries.
The Mediterranean island beneath whose Mount Etna the fire spirit Adranus dwells, whose inhabitants once worshipped him as a god of fire.
The Major Non-Hermetic Virtue of the Seirenes that empowers a character's music to command those who hear it.
A holy Hermetic societas connected to the late Roman sun-cult of it, mentioned as related to the Cult of Mercury.
A Minor Hermetic Flaw in which the character must use casting tools to cast spontaneous spells, with 15 tools one for each Art; only available to Verditius magi.
Patron saint of dyers and weavers; an Egyptian soldier and principal officer of the Theban legion in the third-century Roman army.
The Jerbiton magus who founded and leads Libellus; trained in the Rhine Tribunal, around seventy but looks mid-thirties, with a reputation for risk-taking.
A Virtue suggested as appropriate for Mercurian characters.
A Major Story Flaw in which supernatural entities interfere in the character's life in minor ways, without long-term plans, whenever he is around them.
A Minor General Tainted Virtue: the character has inherited or acquired vast cursed treasure that brings harm and only allows itself to be spent sinfully.
A Major Social Status Virtue for a commander of the Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon with authority over a province or preceptory, also granting Temporal Influence.
A Perdo Mentem 5 spell invented by Imanitos Mendax that renders a target insensate for a moment, registering only the initial touch.
A Rego Terram (ReTe 30) spell opening a chasm; Magic Resistance does not protect against falling in, but does against being crushed when it closes.
The sacred relic brought to Gaul by Mary Magdalene and revealed by Clovis to the Frankish kingdom, later lost when the Merovingian dynasty fell from grace.
A mainly forest-wilderness margravate east of the Elbe bordering Silesia, populated by Sorbs and ruled by the margraves of Meissen.
The greatest waterfalls in Europe near the southeastern edge of the Black Forest, with a central rocky island holding a Magic aura and a regio leading to the Rhine spirit's realm.
A magical beast with Magic Might 10 (Animal), an intelligent bloodhound recruited as covenfolk who can flawlessly track prey and speak; based on the bloodhound from The Book of Mundane Beasts.
Site of a great fair (the it) rivaling Champagne in size and goods; its proximity to Constantinople makes eastern luxuries readily available.
A reclusive young hedge wizard of Waldheim with Latent Magical Ability who befriends forest creatures and is accompanied by the faerie wolf Red-Hame.
A Muto Ignem spell (Level 25) with a Terram requisite that turns the heat and flames of a large campfire into a small hard object such as a gem; breaking the object releases the flame.
An order of monks active since 1198 dedicated to ransoming slaves.
A Major Story Flaw in which the character is one of the it, the 36 hidden righteous on whom the world's continuation relies, destined to face a moment of moral decision.
A small student-run Italian university northwest of Bologna teaching law exclusively, founded by departing Bolognese scholars.
The King of Denmark, relatively secure with Schleswig and Holstein under his control, who in the historical timeline grants Kolding a full charter in 1230.
A weak, Struggling Spring covenant of six magi consisting of tents around a standing stone in a clearing within a faerie-forest magical regio, contesting its sole vis source with faeries.
A Minor Personality Flaw representing a solemn religious obligation, taken by priests for celibacy and by Cathar Perfecti and Mazdean priests for ritual purity.
A Rego Animal 25 warding effect enchanted into Philippus Niger's Subtle Chain.
A Minor Hermetic Flaw in which the magus's Gift is ill attuned to creating enchanted devices, halving Lab Total for creating or investigating enchanted items.
A Major Supernatural Virtue granting a score of 1 in the Supernatural Ability it, letting the character create winds by whistling.
A Minor Supernatural Virtue used by certain Egyptian Sufis interested in calligraphy, allowing them to use unreadable books as sources of training for spiritual subjects.
A Creo Auram Ritual spell (Level 65) that creates an immense hurricane-intensity storm 40 or more miles wide, causing massive damage along shorelines and inland.
entity: Wrath of Whirling Winds and Water
